title: Utaztam, Utaztunk: A New Verb for Travel

sections.title: A regular verb, despite the -ik
sections.content: utazik ("to travel") looks like it might be irregular because of its -ik ending — but unlike eszik and iszik from Unit 24, it's a completely regular verb: utazom, utazol, utazik... in the present, and utaztam, utaztál, utazott... in the past, with no stem change at all. Use it together with a directional case for where you traveled to — Bécsbe utaztunk ("we traveled to Vienna") — the same illative/sublative cases you already use with meglátogat and hazamegy.

items.english: Last summer Károly and I traveled to Vienna.

items.spanish: Ez volt az utolsó nagy utam.
items.english: This was my last big trip.
We traveled by train, because it was cheaper.

sections.content: utazik takes -val/-vel for how you traveled (vonattal, autóval) — the same instrumental case you already use for tools and company, just applied to transport now.
